final.title: When opt-in records stop being trustworthy
final.body:
If your opt-in records stop being trustworthy, treat it as a workflow check before the next send, not as a broad AI project. The simple question is: can you tell, for each contact, whether consent is current, withdrawn, or unclear? If you cannot, do not guess.

In a small business, this often shows up as manual checking, a spreadsheet full of edge cases, or the habit of sending to a list because it is already there. That is where time leaks begin. The approved persona scenario already includes repetitive manual work; messy consent records can become part of that same drag, but that is still a scenario, not a measured result.

One practical next step is to mark each contact as current, stale, or unknown based on the evidence you already have, then keep the stale and unknown group out of the next send. That can be manual, spreadsheet-based, or automation-assisted depending on your tooling. If your email or CRM setup already keeps consent history or supports clean segmentation, use that as the first diagnostic. If it does not, a small workflow check in your own environment can expose the gap.

Human approval stays in the loop for any send decision. Better a boring list review than a polite mistake.
